newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa shares seen knocked by futures next week.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa shares seen knocked by futures next week.

text.p: South African shares, which have put on a bullish guise after a surge in May official reserves a week ago, are likely to come off as market players square-up positions for the June futures contract close-out next week, dealers and portfolio managers said on Friday.
But they added that the market's underlying sentiment would continue to be buoyant, with the financial sector gaining momentum from continued hopes of an interest rate cut.
Early on Friday the financial index continued to climb into positive territory and gained 53.2 points to reach another fresh year high of 9,837.2.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel and reserve bank governor Chris Stals confirmed this week that a slight ease in interest rates, which have hit company earnings by stifling consumer spending, was quite possible later this year.

Latest inflation data reinforced hopes for a cut around August. On Tuesday figures showed all-commodities price producer inflation (CPI) had fallen to 8.8 percent year-on-year in April from 9.6 in March.

"The basket traders are going to force the market down a bit. We think it will be a weakish close-out on the industrials but against that we have quite a bit of positive news such as the Dow which has kept the market higher than it would have been otherwise," Denzil Newman, a portfolio manager at Syfrets Managed Assets, told Reuters.
"We think the financial sector is where interest will remain with this interest rate cut talk," he added.

Portfolio managers said the futures close-out was expected to weigh on shares, but the market should bounce back quickly as fears of a capital flight after the easing of foreign exchange controls on July 1 had also started dissipating.

"I think we have enough reserves at present and I don't think there's going to be a mad rush for foreign assets or currencies," James Scott, an equities trader at stockbroking firm Societe Generale Frankel Pollak told Reuters.

Grahame Graham-Parker, general manager at Infinity Asset Management, added: "I do not think everybody will rush out and run away with money. But (the relaxation) will put downward pressure on the market."
Analysts said there was a dearth of local economic data next week and market players would look at first quarter current accounnt data released on Thursday for some direction.

Responses from 10 economists to a Reuters consensus poll, forecast the current account deficit to increase to an unadjusted 2.1 billion rand compared with a 50 million rand shortfall in the fourth quarter of 1996.

This week has seen another slew of profit warnings from firms complaining they are being squeezed by high interest rates. Technical personnel hire firm Technihire and household goods firm Housewares HWSJ.J both issued gloomy statements.

Next week sees a slew of media firms revealing their figures on Tuesday as Electronic Media Network Ltd (M-Net), M-Cell Ltd, MIH Holdings, Omni Media Corp Ltd and Nasionale Pers Ltd all post year results.
Overall profits are expected to be relatively healthy.
The market is closed on Monday for Youth Day holiday.
